item.title: Cabinet blindsided by Budget 2027 measures against non-EU workers
item.description: The Cabinet was blindsided by the Budget 2027 measures targeting non-EU workers, which introduce higher application and renewal fees and a 400 infrastructure contribution payable by new applicants and resident TCNs who renew their residence. Finance minister Clyde Caruana told parliament the measures would save about 46 million and begin addressing overpopulation. Lawyer Andrew Sciberras and General Workers Union secretary general Kevin Camilleri, among other Labour-aligned figures, criticised the framing of the package, with Sciberras calling it dehumanising and questioning whether it complies with EU law, while Camilleri described the measures as purely populist.
item.content:encoded:
The Cabinet was blindsided by the Budget 2027 measures targeting non-EU workers, which introduce higher application and renewal fees and a 400 infrastructure contribution payable by new applicants and resident TCNs who renew their residence. Finance minister Clyde Caruana told parliament the measures would save about 46 million and begin addressing overpopulation. Lawyer Andrew Sciberras and General Workers Union secretary general Kevin Camilleri, among other Labour-aligned figures, criticised the framing of the package, with Sciberras calling it dehumanising and questioning whether it complies with EU law, while Camilleri described the measures as purely populist.

Sources: Malta Today
